text.insert: Working process flow for this band of the global flow. Confirmed detail from the walkthrough accumulates here before mapping to the owning chapter.

steps.text: `Run Loop` turns the ranked board into landed work
The loop lands work one `Epoch` at a time.
Take a dispatch lease and reconcile sandboxes at startup
Refuse to start without a `--lease-id` and a schedulable run
Clamp `Worker` capacity down to the run's `desiredWorkers`, never up
Repeat each `Epoch` until the run drains, stops, or hits its budget
Open the `Epoch`
Load a candidate window off the knowledge graph
Admit targets from the board once, at `Epoch` open
A fixed `Epoch` takes its size in targets, 64 by default, and is never topped up afterwards. Refill is the next `Epoch`'s job.
Round-robin admission across source files
Rerank the window by model, falling back to priority order
Queue one deduplicated `Worker` job per admitted target
For each admitted target
`Worker` claims the job and its target atomically
Provision an isolated sandbox at the claim's `base_rev`
The claim-time `base_rev` is authoritative for the whole job. Re-reading the loop's current value after a multi-minute provision could name a commit the sandbox never fetched.
`Agent` attempts the target against the sandbox
Repeat run, diff, validate, checkpoint until no repairs remain or the deadline passes
Record a checkpoint on every attempt, passed or not
Gate what leaves the `Worker`
The hard gate is exactly that conjunction: runner validation passed and review lint did not fail. Nothing else feeds it.
Enqueue only the best checkpoint for integration
Integrate the accepted checkpoint into the cycle worktree
Apply single-flight, commit accepted paths, reverse-apply a failed commit
Advance the base revision on every accept
New `Worker`s branch off the latest integration commit, while in-flight `Worker`s keep the base they were provisioned at.
Fan conflicts out into path-disjoint resolvers
Hold resolvers and the `Epoch` boundary against each other
Close the `Epoch` at the boundary once its queue empties
The boundary fires only when the `Epoch` has admitted targets, nothing remaining, nothing claimed, and no `Worker` in flight.
Rebuild report truth in order
Drain the integration queue
Commit a snapshot excluding paths locked by live `Worker`s
Force an incremental report build in the `Epoch` worktree
Read the regression report back
Run full knowledge maintenance against the boundary worktree
Rule on the tentative window
The confirmation pass is opt-in. It reuses the `Epoch`'s own global comparison and runs no build of its own.
Confirm every tentative integration on a clean verdict
Blame only widened candidates on a dirty verdict
Repeat the halving probe until one candidate is left
Probe the singleton alone, then revert only if it convicts
Readmit other regressed targets instead of reverting them
Pause the cycle once regressions cross the threshold
Publish the rebuilt report and advance the baseline
Record a save point as the `Epoch` closes
Cancel still-queued jobs for its targets as `epoch_closed`
Admit the next `Epoch` from the refreshed board
Base new `Worker` worktrees on the boundary commit, compare-and-set
Rerank open target priorities on a fast knowledge refresh
Close an `Epoch` `exhausted` when it admits nothing
Board exhaustion on its own never ends the run: the `Epoch` closes, the loop backs off, and the run ends only on a signal, a drain, the idle limit, or the iteration budget.
Sleep on a resting trigger, then wake and repeat
`Run control` steers the loop from outside while it runs
Settle the run in place, draining the process if it cannot
Stop claiming new `Worker` jobs, let in-flight ones finish
Pause stops intake, not work already claimed.
Demand an explicit confirmation flag for hard stop and recover
Mark the run cancelled with the operator's reason
Force-finish the active `Epoch` without sending a signal
Close active claims, finish open targets, cancel what remains
Pause dispatch on a provider failure, resume on a healthy probe
`SIGINT` and `SIGTERM` stop the loop, `SIGUSR1` drains it
`Shutdown` drains what is in flight before the loop exits
Give in-flight `Worker`s a 30-second grace, then cancel them
`Worker`s ignore `SIGTERM`, so a stopped pool would otherwise wedge for hours waiting on TTLs.
Return every interrupted active target to admitted state
Run one final integration drain before exiting
Await `Epoch` work, resolvers, knowledge lanes, and the provider probe
Set the stop reason from whatever tripped first
